name: std::exchange

declarations.code:
template <class T, class U = T>

T exchange(T &obj, U &&new_value);
declarations.notes: (since C++14) (constexpr since C++20)(conditionally noexcept since C++23)

intro: Replaces the value of obj with new_value and returns the old value of obj.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
obj

 -

 object whose value to replace


 new_value

 -

 the value to assign to obj


 Type requirements


 -T must meet the requirements of MoveConstructible. Also, it must be possible to move-assign objects of type U to objects of type T.

sections.title: Exceptions
sections.text:
(none)


(until C++23)

noexcept specification:  
noexcept(

    std::is_nothrow_move_constructible_v<T> &&

    std::is_nothrow_assignable_v<T&, U>


)

(since C++23)

summary: Replaces the value of obj with new_value and returns the old value of obj.

guides.name: std::exchange
guides.summary: Replace a value and get the old one back.
guides.analogy: Like changing a sign from open to closed while keeping the old sign in your hand.
guides.signature:
template<class T, class U = T>
T exchange(T& object, U&& new_value);
guides.note: This is not an atomic operation. It does not synchronize access between threads.
